heroHeadline: Legislature Rejects Cabinet's NT$210B Special Drone Budget, Passes Own NT$240B Plan (Aug 27); Taiwan Indicts 9 Incl. Nvidia/Super Micro Staff in Chip-Smuggling Crackdown (Aug 25); Cabinet Approves Record NT$1.1225T 2027 Defense Budget (Aug 20); Explosion Injures 13 at Tainan Waste Site (Aug 22); PLA Sorties Fluctuate 0-3/Day Post-Han Kuang 42
heroSubtitle: Since our last full update (July 16), the story has shifted from the summer's headline military moves to a domestic fight over how Taiwan pays for drones. On August 27, the opposition-controlled Legislative Yuan rejected the Cabinet's NT$210 billion (~$6.6B) special budget for roughly 210,000 military drones by 2031, passing a KMT/TPP alternative instead that funds procurement through the regular annual budget — NT$240 billion (~$7.6B) over six years, NT$40 billion/year with room to grow. President Lai had urged the special budget's passage a day earlier, invoking lessons from Ukraine and the Middle East; Defense Minister Wellington Koo warns the NT$40B annual cap is insufficient, and Premier Cho Jung-tai has not said whether the Cabinet will countersign. On the chip-smuggling front, Keelung prosecutors indicted nine people on August 25 — including an Nvidia Taiwan employee and two Super Micro Taiwan staff — over an alleged scheme to smuggle 74 Nvidia-equipped AI servers to China via Japan, Indonesia and Hong Kong (56 more were intercepted at customs), building on the Super Micro-linked raids that began in July. On the defense-budget side, the Cabinet formally approved a record NT$1.1225 trillion 2027 defense allocation on August 20 — the first year above NT$1 trillion, extending President Lai's push toward 5% of GDP by 2030. Away from policy, an explosion and fire at a waste-storage site in Tainan's Annan District injured 13 people (three firefighters, ten residents) on August 22; no fatalities were reported. PLA activity itself stayed within its post-Han Kuang 42 pattern: after a first-ever zero-sortie day on August 21, sorties rebounded to 3/day on August 22-23 (all crossing the median line) before easing to 2 on August 24, continuing to fluctuate well below the June 4 all-time non-exercise high of 32. TSMC's rally continued on strong AI demand — July monthly revenue hit NT$467.58 billion (+45% YoY, reported August 10) — while the $14 billion US arms package remains 'under review' with no new public resolution since June.
